deep.reconstruction:
Context. The neighbouring pages concern a system of pseudo-lines in the real projective plane, drawn in the disc model: a circle with antipodal identification. A distinguished polygon, with vertices indexed by Z/NZ (or the 2n ends of n pseudo-lines on the boundary circle), is carried around by 'parallel transport'. Crossing a face F_n to F_{n+1} acts on Z/NZ by a reflection sigma_n(t) = l_n - t. A product of p reflections is (-1)^p (t - chi_p), where chi_p is an alternating sum of the l_i. For p = 2n this gives the translation lambda(t) = t - (n-1). The next page (dated 3.1.83) uses this to bound the image of pi_1 of the configuration space in the dihedral group D_{2n}. It then turns to the sign character chi: D_{2n} -> {+1, -1}. That sign depends on the parity of the number of 'steps' (pivots of a pseudo-line about a vertex) needed for a half-turn. The text says explicitly 'on aimerait pouvoir le faire en un nb pair de pas'.

This page is a scratch sheet, written on the back of a recycled Montpellier computer-centre listing dated 17 Aug 1982.
(1) Top line: a step count. Read as nu(n-1) + nu(n-3), the line runs through crossed-out attempts (2nu n - 3nu, nu(2n-3)) to the boxed result 2nu(n-2). Beside it is the bare count 2(n-2). This is plausibly the number of elementary steps in a half-turn made of nu rounds of two kinds, of lengths n-1 and n-3. The total is even, which is what the sign computation wants. The reading is a reconstruction; it depends on deciphering the operator sign.
(2) Green U-shaped 'half-polygon' diagrams labelled (3,5), (3,4), (3,3). Each is a straight top edge (a segment of the line at infinity or the pivot line) over a curved chain carrying 5, 4 or 3 marked vertices. Below, a periodic pattern '---(3,4)(3,3)(3,4)---' is drawn with braces marked '1-' / '-1'. This suggests the types of successive faces met during transport repeat periodically, with the vertex count changing by plus or minus 1 at each step. That matches the earlier relation l_s - l_a = nu_t - 1.
(3) Circle diagrams. The boundary circle carries thick black arcs (blocks of line-ends at infinity) and red hatch marks labelled '1/1'. One circle shows a pseudo-line as an ellipse-like arc from '+' at the top to '-' at the bottom; another circle has green dots for vertices. These are pictures of rotating a pseudo-line about a vertex and tracking how its endpoints sweep the boundary blocks.
(4) Small labelled polygons: a pentagon with vertices 0-4 and a quadrilateral with vertices 0-3 (beside a small 3-D-looking sketch labelled 1, 2, 3). These illustrate the Z/NZ labelling on which the reflections act.

Purpose: count the steps of a half-turn (it comes out even, 2nu(n-2)), so as to decide the sign component of the monodromy of the distinguished polygon under pi_1 of the space of pseudo-line systems.
errors: The top computation shows false starts (2nu n - 3nu, nu(2n-3)), crossed out before the boxed 2nu(n-2). This is consistent with nu(n-1) + nu(n-3) = 2nu(n-2), but not with the '-' sign in the machine transcription: nu(n-1) - nu(n-3) = 2nu. Either the sign is a '+' or the line was rewritten.
No argument is given on this page that a half-turn really decomposes into nu(n-1) + nu(n-3) steps. The parity conclusion rests on that unproved decomposition.

ideas.what: Monodromy of the labelling of a polygon or face (Z/NZ) under transport through a sequence of faces. Each crossing is a reflection t -> l - t, and products are translations by alternating sums.
ideas.modern_name: Dihedral monodromy action of the fundamental group of a configuration/realization space of pseudo-line arrangements
ideas.usually_credited_to: Pseudo-line arrangements: Levi (1926), Ringel (1956), Goodman-Pollack (1980s). The topology of the corresponding spaces: Mnev (1988) and later work on oriented matroids.
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA. The pseudo-line project is at most alluded to in his mid-1980s writings; unsure.

ideas.what: Counting the elementary pivot steps (rotating a pseudo-line about a vertex) in a half-turn, to get the sign character D_{2n} -> {+1, -1}: total 2nu(n-2), even.
ideas.modern_name: Mutation / triangle-flip sequences (Ringel moves); parity of flip sequences
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ringel (1956) for connectivity by flips; Goodman-Pollack for allowable sequences

ideas.what: Periodic pattern of face types (3,4)(3,3)(3,4)... with the vertex count changing by plus or minus 1 along a transport path.
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorics of faces swept by a rotating line (sweeps of arrangements)

missed.claim: Grothendieck aims to determine the image of pi_1 of the space of pseudo-line systems (and of a cover of it) in the dihedral group D_{2n} acting on a distinguished 2n-gon. He has shown the image contains Z/nZ with index at most 4. The sign component remains open and he tries to settle it by step parity; this page computes an even count 2nu(n-2). I know of no published treatment of this dihedral monodromy question for pseudo-line arrangement spaces.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Monodromy and fundamental groups of realization spaces of oriented matroids are an active topic (universality, flip graphs). An explicit dihedral monodromy invariant would be a small but concrete computation. The page itself, however, is a fragmentary scratch computation.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a scratch sheet: one step count (2nu(n-2), even), schematic face-type diagrams, and circle pictures of pivoting pseudo-lines. It serves the monodromy computation of the adjacent pages. It belongs to an under-documented Grothendieck project, but no finished result appears here.
transcription_corrections: Top line: the operator between nu(n-1) and nu(n-3) is most plausibly '+', which the boxed 2nu(n-2) requires. The intermediate expressions 2nu n - 3nu and nu(2n-3) are crossed out. The '2' under nu(n-1) is a separate mark, not necessarily a denominator.
'+ / i' is a '+' at the top and a '-' at the bottom of an arc: a pseudo-line through antipodal boundary points, not the letter i.
The labels '1/-1' and '1/1' beside the large circle are hand annotations of boundary blocks (possibly '1/1' or 'n/1'); uncertain.
'0 1 2 3 4' labels the vertices of a pentagon; '0 1 2 3' (with 1, 2, 3 near a small 3-D-looking sketch) labels a quadrilateral, not free-standing numbers.
Braces marked '1-' and '-1' accompany the (3,4)(3,3)(3,4) half-polygon diagrams, indicating a vertex count changing by plus or minus 1.

The printed matter is a recycled banner listing for job 296 named 'CRAY2', run 17 Aug 1982 at a Montpellier computing centre (French operator notices). 'CRAY2' is a job or user name, not the Cray-2 machine. The listing gives a terminus post quem of Aug 1982.
